title: Chirps and Chatter
subtitle: Those hinges ... they're in need of some refinements!

items.text: Afternoon of the Next Day
Central Nave, Cathedral Interior

items.speaker: Alberto
items.text: Is that you, Mr. Leonardo?!

items.speaker: Alberto
items.text: Thank God! I still hadn't truly believed the rumors of your return.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: I know. *sigh* There was some trouble in Milan.

items.speaker: Alberto
items.text: We've heard about the scandal concerning Duke Sforza. How savage ...

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: That's why I came back, with a creative fever inspired by my pains.
The old priest gasps as if the young painter's words stung his ears.

items.speaker: Alberto
items.text: I see ... So, then have you come to finish the Assumption of Mary?

items.speaker: Alberto
items.text: It's been four years since you left. We've been careful to leave it untouched. Now, by the light of the Lord, you're finally back ...

items.speaker: Alberto
items.text: We emptied the Duomo as you requested. I promise no one will bother you.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Thank you. I must get to work right away. My inspiration may fade at any moment.

items.speaker: Alberto
items.text: Hmm, but who are these ladies?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Good day, Father. I am here as Mr. Leonardo's apprentice.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: And uhm ... why, why ... I'm here to evaluate his work for my father, of course!

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Allow me to present, Father Alberto, Miss Sotheby Domenico.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: She's provided huge support for my art career, so, to show my gratitude, I've asked her to model.

items.speaker: Alberto
items.text: For the Assumption of Mary?!
The old priest dabs a bead of sweat off of his forehead unconsciously.

items.speaker: Alberto
items.text: This lady is a bit young, don't you think? And not exactly how I had pictured Mary ...

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Who is the artist, Father? Do not let your mind be so entrenched by outdated styles.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: When you look for a model, you must focus on their soul not simply their flesh! You pay too much attention to her appearance, yet neglect what's inside.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: The Assumption of Mary depicts the Madonna's reception into heaven, not just in body but in spirit as well.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: And what do you think best captures that moment, Father?

items.speaker: Alberto
items.text: Umm ... Ehh ...

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Huh?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Hmm? Why are you looking at me?
Leonardo gestures at Sotheby, presenting her like a showman.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Right! That innocence and vitality! She may be a little young, but her spirit is perfect ...

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: In fact, it is that innocence which makes her more qualified than anyone! She will be indispensable for my work. For my inspiration, you know ...

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Huh? Oh, well. Then, I must thank you for your compliment, Mr. Leonardo.

items.speaker: Alberto
items.text: You have convinced me once again, Leonardo! Although something tells me that we should go deeper into this topic ...

items.speaker: Alberto
items.text: Another time perhaps; for now I will trust in your piety and capability. Please let me know if you need anything else.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: As it happens, there is something, Father.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: You see, I would like to try some new perspective techniques on this work. I know that Paolo Uccello is a master of perspective. Do you have any of his works around?

items.speaker: Alberto
items.text: Yes! Saint George and the Dragon. One of his masterpieces.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Ah, but I have already seared this one into my mind! Have you any others?

items.speaker: Alberto
items.text: Hmm ... yes, there's another fresco in the dome, but it was suspended midway by the sponsor, the Arte della Lana.

items.speaker: Alberto
items.text: More than a dozen artisans and artists, including Mr. Uccello, the chief painter, participated in this project, but none of them received a single florin for their work. God bless them ...

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Oh ... How terrible. Those poor artists.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: What happened?

items.speaker: Alberto
items.text: This was nearly 20 years ago ... I suppose it was simply too expensive. The dome itself is rarely visited.

items.speaker: Alberto
items.text: It is only natural that our money go to the central nave, where all the faithful might see it.

items.speaker: Alberto
items.text: I should leave you to your work, sir. God bless you all.
Alberto crosses his heart and leaves.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Phew ... They're finally gone. Alright, time to start Operation Florence Typhon!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Wait, where's Vertin?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Right behind you.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Oh! Where did you go? We're about to get started.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I wanted to make sure that there was no one else in the cathedral before we began. I believe we are alone now.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We shouldn't be disturbed for some time.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: It's always good to be cautious, miss!

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: I should signal Ezio and Mr. APPLe now. They've waited long enough.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Is there something wrong, Vertin? You don't look well.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm fine. I'm not used to the smells here ...

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: The smells? *sniff* It's frankincense ... *sniff* and myrrh!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Those are the most prominent ones I can detect; I believe there may be some other local florals ...

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: I wonder if all the incense is meant to make you dizzy on purpose! What better way is there to see clouds and angels ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That's a clever theory.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: But heavy incense can certainly be unpleasant for some people ... Oh, but Miss Sotheby has the perfect thing to help.
She flings open her bag and retrieves a potion.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Apply two drops just inside your nose, and you should be right as rain!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Thank you.
Nearby Rooftop, Cathedral Exterior

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: The weather is truly lovely today, isn't it?
The golden apple basks cozily beneath the Tuscan sun.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Any sign of the signal yet?

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: ... Not yet.
A short time later, the assassin makes his way to the apple's side.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: There's a window near the ribs; we should be able to sneak in through there.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Marvelous! All that's left to do is to wait for their signal.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Mmm, the sun is so warm and gentle right now, like sipping a cup of fresh-made Cornish tea. Ouch!
*chirp*

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: A bird? Did it think this APPLe was a fine-looking snack?

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Hmm? It has letters on it ... itnava?

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Let me see.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: It's mirrored font, one of Leonardo's codes. You reverse it to get the true message: avanti ...

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: "Action."

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Oh! I see, nothing too complex. But what about this bird?

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Another of his bizarre inventions. It has to hit something to stop.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: You should be thankful; he's improved it from his last design. It used to fly so fast that it would knock you off your feet.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Remarkable! It is an amazing invention. If I were you, I would suggest that he take good care of all his blueprints so they might be passed down in the future.
Ezio smiles.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: It wouldn't do any good. His genius may well be forgotten since he guards his ideas so jealously—he writes everything in ciphers like this.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: He would rather see his work burn than have someone else complete it for him.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: He won't worry about the future until it comes. That's just his way.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: And what about you, Ezio?
The Assassin looks down at his own shadow.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: I am an Assassin. We work in the dark to serve the light. I don't want to be remembered.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: That sounds lonely ... Do you mind if I ask something? You've avoided speaking about your family, it sounds like something terrible happened.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Are they why you became an Assassin?

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: It is a long story ... my father and brothers were killed by the Templars.
The Assassin covers his face beneath his hood and replies in a soft voice.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: I was only 17 ... So much has changed since then. I've changed.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: I'm terribly sorry, Ezio. Forgive me, I should never have brought it up ...
APPLe falls silent, for a moment it almost seems as if his golden skin loses its shine.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: It's not your fault.
His eyes trace the flight of an eagle in the distance. Then he turns and his face seems as gloomy as midnight.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: It was three in the morning.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: I placed their bodies on a boat, performed their last rites and then lit their pyre. I watched as it drifted away down the Arno.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: The pride of the Auditores, yet I couldn't even bury them properly.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: All I could do was keep my enemies' names in mind ... Vieri de' Pazzi, Francesco de' Pazzi, Uberto Alberti ...

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: I took their lives, every last one of them.
The wind blows away a painful sigh.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: I don't think I've told anyone that for a long time.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: I can't imagine the pain ... not to mention how hard it must have been to overcome it.
He shakes his head with a bitter smile.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: I didn't. You don't overcome that sort of pain ... No, I took it in and made it part of myself.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: I feel it again, raw and new, every time I draw my blade. It's always there, guiding me from each target to the next.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: But you said that "Assassins only kill for a just cause." Isn't that just killing for revenge?
Ezio looks out from his hood with a cold stare.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Revenge can be a just cause if it rights injustice—I have to believe that.
Footsteps disturb a nearby tile.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Someone's here.
Ezio grabs APPLe and moves like a shadow behind a nearby chimney.
Not long after two Templars round the edge of the roof.

items.speaker: Templar III
items.text: Damn! The whole Duomo has been blocked for some "honored guest."

items.speaker: Templar III
items.text: Even Mr. Rodrigo can't get us in. I didn't know we'd sunk this low.

items.speaker: Templar IV
items.text: What are we even on the lookout for? Some kind of apple? Is it related to the relics?

items.speaker: Templar IV
items.text: Ugh ...

items.speaker: Templar III
items.text: What now?
The other Templar reaches for his neck.

items.speaker: Templar IV
items.text: A poisoned arro- ...
He falls to the ground before finishing the words.

items.speaker: Templar III
items.text: What?!

items.speaker: Templar III
items.text: Assassin ... Assassin over here!!

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: That should be the last one.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: But the Templars will be on high alert. We need to hurry.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Yes, sir.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: *cough* It's ... It's dusty in here. Are you sure this is the right way, Ezio?

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: It's the only one that isn't crawling with Templars, so it has to be. *cough*

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: I guess that's a good point.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Look ... There's light ahead.
They find a narrow stairway after moving around the corner. A beam of light illuminates the space through the vent.
Secret Tunnel, Cathedral Interior

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Oh, who would have guessed? A secret tunnel!

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Let's go, friend.
It's clear no one has been here for a long time, yet a sense of danger chokes the air.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: The brick patterning ... It's like nothing I've ever seen before.
The dome's bricks are arranged diagonally, layered all the way into the shadow at the top.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: We call it the spina di pesce, herringbone. Another of Brunelleschi's innovations.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: I know next to nothing about architecture, but Leonardo would say it helps to carry the weight of the dome.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: That makes perfect sense! The diagonal arrangement must prevent them from shifting under the immense weight. A positively genius design!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: And to realize it the bricks must have been layered with incredible precision.
APPLe sighs unconsciously.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: That would explain why it took so long to complete.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Sixteen years ... I'm certain it must have been exciting to witness its completion after so much time.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Brunelleschi, Leonardo, Uccello ... Your hometown is full of amazing people, Ezio.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: This APPLe wishes he had been born here.
Ezio turns looking over the wall.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: There's no city quite like Firenze.
Like a row of steadfast soldiers, the bricks extend upward as the Assassin climbs the stairs.
Like silent observers over the course of history.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: What's wrong?

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: There's something on the wall.
Several humanoid symbols have been hidden in a nook.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: These appear to be the same symbols from the manuscript.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Then we're on the right path.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Look. Another symbol over there!
One pursuer, two pursuers, three ...
The symbols appear one after another, as if guiding the way.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: We must be close. Action ...
He speeds up his pace.
After turning several corners, Ezio spots a beam of light—
The symbols converge on a single destination.
What lies ahead? An answer, or more questions?
Ezio takes a deep breath and walks into the dazzling light.
The blinding light slowly dims, giving way to the gentle warmth of candlelight.
When he opens his eyes again he sees several discolored frescoes.
In the middle of these silent figures, flowers, and birds; a blank space.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: So, this is ... the secret chamber?
